messages:
alex: Heads up — EU-NORTH edge is seeing a spike in tail latency (p95 -> 3.2s) and some requests are timing out. Noticing a lot of batcher requeues.
maria: I see a corresponding error in the runtime logs: KV serialization timeouts and socket write errors to the edge fabric. Example: `kvcache: serialize: timeout after 1200ms` and `write: broken pipe` in the same timeframe.
sasha: Confirmed. Continuous-batcher queues jumped and then stalled. Autoscaler attempts to spin up new GPU nodes but cloud reports CP capacity errors (no GPUs available in eu-north zone).
ajay: Can we divert traffic to na1/dedicated pools? Capacity there is healthy. We should avoid broad failover if it's just fabric between edge and cache tier.
alex: Plan: 1) throttle incoming max_concurrency on EU-NORTH to reduce batching pressure. 2) disable continuous batching for 30m for that region. 3) route non-SLO traffic to NA1 via route override. 4) try kernel-level backoff on KV serializer.
maria: I'm applying throttling on the ingress controller now: `kubectl patch config ingress -p '{"spec":{"max_concurrency": 60}}'` — will monitor.
ajay: Pushing traffic reroute: set route policy for eu-north to prefer na1 for model=llama-13b, fallback probability 80%: `/routes patch --region eu-north --rule 'prefer:na1 p=0.8 model:llama-13b'`
deploy-bot: Deployment triggered: route-policy-update v2 by ajay at 1767012402 :rocket:
sasha: I disabled continuous batching on the runtime nodes in eu-north: `PATCH /runtime/config {"continuous_batching": false}` — dropping batch wait windows to 0ms. This reduces throughput but should clear KV lock contention.
maria: KV cache team reports a spike in serialization queuing tied to a recent runtime change (PR #4579) that changed buffer pooling. Rolling that change back on one canary pool now.
alex: Good. Rollback command acknowledged. Can someone comment on client-visible impact? Expected p95 after measures?
ajay: After throttling + reroute + disabling continuous batching p95 dropped from 3.2s -> ~650ms in the last 4m. Error rate down from 1.8% -> 0.3%.
sasha: Still seeing occasional `io: write timeout` anomalies on a small subset of edge nodes — taking those nodes OOS and will reprovision.
maria: Canary rollback complete on pool-eu-north-1. Monitoring for KV queuing. Logs show serialization latencies back to baseline.
oncall-bot: Incident update: EU-NORTH partial degradation. Mitigations applied: ingress throttling, traffic reroute, batching disabled, canary rollback. Next check in 10m.
alex: Thx. Followups: 1) revert route after 60m if stable, 2) postmortem to capture root cause (buffer pooling change + fabric errors + capacity squeeze), 3) consider autoscaler fallback behaviors when cloud returns capacity errors.
ajay: I'll open a follow-up ticket for autoscaler fallback logic + capacity-aware reroute. Tagging infra-schedulers.
maria: I'll start the postmortem draft and attach relevant logs/commands. Adding timeline.
sasha: Removing two unhealthy edge nodes now: `nodes cordon node-eu-12 && drain node-eu-12` — reprovision queued.
alex: Great. If p95 stays <1s for 15m, we'll move to recovery state and gradually re-enable continuous batching with conservative settings.
maria: recovery-looking-good at 1767012479, p95 720ms and falling. I'll update the incident channel and PMs.
alex: Nice work team :thumbsup:"
